text:
The Fed didn't cut rates to zero in 2024. It cut three times, starting in September, and ended the year at 4.25-4.50%, down from 5.25-5.50%: 50 bp in September, then 25 bp each in November and December.

The cuts came because inflation had fallen substantially toward the 2% target while the labor market was cooling (slower hiring, rising unemployment). That shifted the Fed's priority from fighting inflation to avoiding unnecessary damage to employment, so it began easing policy from a restrictive level.

You may be thinking of the zero-bound episodes in December 2008 and March 2020 (the financial crisis and COVID), when emergency cuts took the rate to 0-0.25%.
